name: Mzuri Wildlife Foundation Wildlife Conservation Grants
summary: Small grants for grassroots wildlife conservation work such as habitat enhancement and anti-poaching. Applicants send a letter of inquiry first, then are invited to submit a formal application.
reporting: Grantees report on progress against the goals, objectives and outcomes in their proposal.

calls.label: Yearly cycle: LOI 15 September, application 1 November
calls.recurring: Letter of inquiry due 15 September; invited formal applications accepted in the fourth quarter, due 1 November.

status.quote: Letter of Inquiry Deadline: September 15th Formal Grant Application Deadline: November 1st

recurring.quote: Formal grant applications are accepted only in the fourth quarter of each calendar year for consideration in the first quarter of the following year. Please follow the steps below to apply for funding. Letter of Inquiry Deadline: September 15th Formal Grant Application Deadline: November 1st

applicant_types.quote: Proof of the organization's tax-exemption or proof of a U.S.-based fiscal sponsor.

geography.quote: Partnering with grassroots organizations around the world, we are working to reverse this trend.

access.quote: We invite grant applicants to submit brief letters of inquiry as outlined below.

window.quote: Letter of Inquiry Deadline: September 15th Formal Grant Application Deadline: November 1st

amount.quote: Grant awards typically range in size from $5000 to $15,000
